text:
The Flyers' month has been about Matvei Michkov more than any result. ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported Michkov would likely want a fresh start elsewhere. GM Daniel Briere said that report was not correct after meeting the player and his agent, Rick Tocchet called it untrue, and multiple outlets reported Michkov has not requested a trade. A heated bench exchange with Nick Seeler didn't help the noise. Michkov, a restricted free agent after this season, leads the team in goals.

On the ice, Philadelphia beat Buffalo 4-3 on Tuesday, a game Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports called a good win built on two strong periods. At 7-11-6 the Flyers sit well back, and the finishing is the main reason. They've scored more than 11 fewer goals than their chances earned, the kind of shortfall that makes a 46% expected-goals team (the quality of chances) look worse than it is. Over the last ten games they've had 52%, which is better than the record.

The Noah Cates, Michkov and Porter Martone line has the best chance share of the regulars at 62%, though Martone, the rookie, is running cold with 3 points against 5.5 expected in his last ten. Travis Sanheim and Jamie Drysdale are the reliable pair. Our playoff odds are 7%. The story to watch is whether this group, and Michkov's place in it, settles down.
